title: “Round the World.”
subtitle: Letters from Japan, China, India, and Egypt
omitted_from_reading: The printed contents and the errata leaf are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: The corrections in the book’s errata leaf are made in the text, each marked as a correction.
summary: Wm. Perry Fogg of Cleveland, Ohio, left home in the autumn of 1870 to see “the strange and curious nations of the Orient,” and wrote these letters to the Cleveland Leader, where they first appeared. He went by rail to Salt Lake City and San Francisco, by steamer to Japan, where seven letters describe Yokohama, Kamakura, Yeddo, the Inland Sea, and Nagasaki, and on to Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canton, Singapore, and Penang. He crossed India from Calcutta by Benares, Lucknow, Agra, and Delhi to the hills at Mussoorie and Simla and to Bombay, and ended in Egypt, at Cairo and the Pyramids. The book was printed in 1872 as a souvenir for his friends, not for sale, with mounted photographs and a list of errata for the newspaper's misprints.
